chunks: Al-Shaykh al-Jalil Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, may God have mercy on him, said: My father, may God be pleased with him, narrated to me saying: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far al-Kamandani narrated to us saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ash'ari narrated to us saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran narrated to us, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, peace be upon him, who said:

God, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Adam, peace be upon him: O Adam, I shall gather all goodness for you in four sayings: one of them is for Me, one is for you, one is between Me and you, and one is between you and the people. As for that which is for Me, you shall worship Me and not associate anything with Me. As for that which is for you, I shall reward you for your deeds when you are most in need of it. As for that which is between Me and you, upon you is the supplication and upon Me is the response. And as for that which is between you and the people, be pleased for the people with what you are pleased with for yourself.

key_terms.تَرْضَى لِنَفْسِكَ: you are pleased with for yourself

ai.seo_question: What are the four divine principles that God revealed to Prophet Adam according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam al-Baqir (AS) relates a divine revelation to Prophet Adam (AS) in which God distills all goodness into four comprehensive principles: (1) pure monotheistic worship without associating partners with God, (2) divine reward for good deeds at the time of greatest need (i.e., the Day of Judgment), (3) a covenant of supplication and divine response between God and the servant, and (4) the golden rule of treating others as one wishes to be treated. This teaching was delivered as part of the earliest divine guidance to humanity through Adam, establishing fundamental ethical and theological principles that would be reiterated by all subsequent prophets.
